text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered — High QPS spike for org opalnet (org_id: op-0pal-123). Error rate creeping up (502s + 429s). Auto-mitigation applied: org-level throttles. Severity: P1. https://incidents.redwood/1767504321

alex_oncall: grabbing this. are they failing customer-side or just seeing throttles?

jen_sre: 3x baseline qps to /v1/generate from op-0pal-123. Most errors are 429s from per-org RL; a few 502s when backend queues overloaded. Burst started ~2m ago and is sustained.

alex_oncall: customer impact? SLA risk?

luis_pm: OpalNet reports editor timeouts and failed saves — user-visible. They have an active marketing push, so traffic burst is expected. SLA is 99.9. Need to reduce user visible errors now.

nora_eng: recommendation: temporary emergency RL bump + traffic shaping. Proposal: bump org RL 200 qps -> 600 qps for 8 minutes, expand burst window to 60s (from 10s), and route non-critical calls to redwood-compact-v1 (cheaper, lower latency). Also flip off heavy attachments feature flag for the org.

alex_oncall: sounds reasonable. any objections?

jen_sre: +1 to bump but we must cap cost exposure and set immediate rollback trigger if backend latency/p50/p95 or 5xx spikes beyond thresholds. Capture traces for a sample of failed requests.

ops-bot: Executing RL update now:
```
POST /admin/orgs/op-0pal-123/rate_limit
{ "qps": 600, "burst_window_s": 60, "duration_s": 480 }
```

ops-bot: Success — RL updated for org op-0pal-123 -> 600 qps for 8m. change_id=rlchg-9876 :white_check_mark:

nora_eng: toggling feature flag to disable heavy multimodal attachments for opalnet: ff.opalnet_heavy_attachments = false

ops-bot: Feature flag updated. Notifying downstream routing.

nora_eng: also starting model routing: 30% of calls to redwood-compact-v1 for this org to reduce token/time costs.

ops-bot: Applying model routing change:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/orgs/op-0pal-123/routing 
-H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP' 
-d '{ "route": [{"model":"redwood-compact-v1","pct":30}, {"model":"redwood-v1","pct":70}] }'
```

ops-bot: Model routing applied. 30% -> redwood-compact-v1. change_id=rout-4521

alex_oncall: set watch: alert if 5xx > 0.5% OR cost delta > 30% vs baseline. Also schedule auto-rollback in 8m. Handing off monitoring to night on-call in 20m: @sara_oncall please pick up and confirm rollback. :alarm_clock:

sara_oncall: ack — I'll monitor metrics and confirm rollback at T+8m (or earlier if we hit rollback triggers).

jen_sre: collecting top prompt samples and traces for post-incident analysis. Will add to timeline.

luis_pm: I’ll send a customer-facing update: "We applied a temporary rate increase and routing changes to reduce user errors; monitoring closely and will follow up with timeline and root cause."

ops-bot: Customer notification queued to support channel and Ops Slack DM.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation in place, lowering severity to P2 (customer errors reduced). Next update in 10 minutes or on notable change.

alex_oncall: summary of actions: 1) RL bump to 600 qps for 8m (rlchg-9876) 2) expanded burst_window to 60s 3) disabled heavy attachments FF 4) routing 30% -> redwood-compact-v1 (rout-4521). Owners: oncall/alex, eng/nora, sre/jen, pm/luis.

jen_sre: postmortem owners assigned; will include tuning per-org burst windows and better per-org RWQ monitoring.

sara_oncall: will confirm rollback and close once metrics stable post-rollback.

luis_pm: thanks team. I'll coordinate a customer debrief after postmortem. :thumbsup:
